statement: A lamp starts off. Each button press switches it on or off. Monday to Friday, Ivy presses it 2, 1, 1, 2 and 2 times. On how many days is it on at bedtime?

choices.misconception: I counted the days when she pressed an odd number of times that day, Tuesday and Wednesday, and forgot the lamp keeps its state from the day before.
I counted the days when she pressed an even number of times that day, because I thought even meant on.
I thought the lamp started on, so I counted the days it would be on if it began on, which are the days it is really off.
I thought every press turns the lamp on, so it is on every day.

hints: The lamp does not reset at night. Keep a running count.
Two presses bring the lamp back to how it was. So only the total number of presses so far matters: an odd total means on, an even total means off.
The totals at bedtime are 2, then 3, then 4, then 6, then 8. Look for the odd totals.

solutions.reliable: Add up the presses as the week goes on. Monday: 2 presses in all, off. Tuesday: 3, on. Wednesday: 4, off. Thursday: 6, off. Friday: 8, off. The lamp is on at bedtime only on Tuesday, so the answer is 1 day. The idea to keep: a switch that flips each time is decided by whether the total number of flips is odd or even.
solutions.elegant: Track the lamp itself: off, then 2 presses keep it off; 1 press turns it on; 1 press turns it off; 2 presses keep it off; 2 presses keep it off. It was on only after Tuesday. Pairs of presses cancel, so only the odd days change anything.

whyOnTest: Flipping a switch is odd and even in disguise: an odd number of flips changes it, an even number leaves it as it was.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
